notes:
**Windows** — run `ruze_0.0.66_x64-setup.exe`.
**macOS** — open `ruze_0.0.66_universal.dmg` and drag Ruze into Applications. macOS 12 or newer, Apple Silicon or Intel. Ruze is not notarized by Apple, so the first time macOS will refuse to open it: go to System Settings → Privacy & Security, and choose *Open Anyway* beside the message about Ruze.
**Linux** — `flatpak install ruze-0.0.66.flatpak`, then `flatpak run com.ruze.chat`.
**Android** — sideload `ruze-0.0.66.apk`. arm64 devices, Android 8.0 or newer.
**iOS** — sideload `ruze-0.0.66.ipa` with AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly, which sign it with your own Apple ID. iOS 15 or newer. Ruze is not on the App Store; with a free Apple ID the install has to be refreshed every seven days, which those tools do for you.
**Server hosting** — not the app. The `ruze-server-` files are ruzed, for a machine you run: hosting for your servers, so messages reach people who were offline, a relay, or both — you choose when you install it. On Linux, `ruze-server-0.0.66-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` (or `-aarch64`); on a Mac, `ruze-server-0.0.66-macos-universal.tar.gz`, Apple Silicon or Intel, macOS 11 or newer; the README inside each says how to set it up. On Windows, `ruze-server-0.0.66-windows-x86_64-setup.exe`, which installs it as a service.

---

Files sent from a phone can be downloaded once the phone is put away, your
messages show where they have got to, and the server column is clearer.

### Added

- **Your messages in a server show whether they have been delivered.** Beside
  the time of each message you send: a clock while it is only on your
  device, one tick once the server's VPS has it, and two green ticks once
  somebody else's device does. Point at the mark to see who. Under a file you
  sent, a line says where the file is: "Uploading to the server — keep Ruze
  open on this device", then "On the server", and who has downloaded it. In
  a server with no VPS it says the file is only on your device until somebody
  downloads it. A copy somebody got from the VPS or from another member is
  not counted, because it never touched your device. Conversations with
  friends still show the clock only.

### Changed

- **The open server's column is easier to read.** Channels sit under a
  "Text channels" label with a # before each, and voice channels under
  "Voice" with a speaker, all in rows of one height. The channel you are
  reading has a shaded background in every theme; on the light theme it
  used to be shown only by a change of colour in its name. The server's
  name is a header with a line under it and an arrow saying it opens the
  server's menu, and its connection dot sits on the corner of its picture.
  An empty voice channel is a row like any other; one with people in it
  keeps its card, now marked with a green "Live" label. "Start a live chat"
  is a quiet outlined row at the end of the voice list instead of the
  loudest thing in the column. If you own the server, a + beside "Text
  channels" creates a new one.

- **Hovering over a server on the rail shows a card of what is happening
  there.** It has the server's name and picture, and then: how many
  mentions and unread messages are waiting for you, or that you are all
  caught up; who is talking in its voice channels, for servers whose rooms
  this device has seen; and whether this device is syncing with anyone. It
  comes up straight away, beside the server it belongs to, and also when
  you move along the rail with the keyboard. Before, the same facts were a
  single line of text that appeared after a second's wait, run together
  with dashes.

### Fixed

- **A file sent from a phone can be downloaded after the phone is put
  away.** A file stayed on the device that sent it until somebody downloaded
  it, and downloading asked that device alone — so a video shared from a
  phone with Ruze in the background failed to download for everyone. Now the
  sending device uploads each file to the server's VPS as soon as it is
  sent, and keeps trying until the VPS has it. A download asks the VPS first,
  then the sender, then other members who may already have it. The VPS
  accepts files only from members of the servers it holds. **Update ruzed on
  your VPS to 0.0.66** for uploads to work. Until then files still download
  from the sender, and from members who already have them.
- **Two live chats are no longer both called "Live channel 1".** A room you
  start without a name is numbered from the rooms your device can see, and
  it may not see them all yet — somebody who has just come in, or two people
  starting one at the same moment — so two rooms could share a number with
  nothing to tell them apart. Now one keeps it and the other takes the next
  free number, and every device agrees which is which. Rooms somebody named
  themselves are left as they are.
